regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code (식품공전) — Ministry of Food and Drug Safety
notes: Korea Food Code closely mirrors Codex GSFA limits for most additives.

regulatory_basis: BPOM Regulation No. 11 of 2019 — Food Additives
notes: Indonesia closely follows Codex GSFA. Halal status of carrier solvents must also be verified.

regulatory_basis: Thai FDA Notification on Food Additives — Preservatives
notes: Thailand sets stricter limits than Codex for some beverages. Thai FDA publishes approved additive list with specific food category limits.

regulatory_basis: Food Regulations 1985 (Malaysia) — First Schedule
notes: Malaysia Food Regulations set limits; products must also comply with Halal requirements if Halal-certified.

regulatory_basis: Philippine National Standard (PNS) / FDA-PH Food Additive Regulations
notes: Philippines follows Codex GSFA. FDA-PH published updated additive regulations in 2019.

regulatory_basis: QCVN 4-10:2010/BYT — National Technical Regulation on Preservatives
notes: Vietnam's 2010 food additive regulation. Some limits differ from Codex. Updates ongoing to align with ASEAN harmonisation.

regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code — Food Coloring Standards
notes: Korea requires labelling of all permitted food colours by name. No EU-style hyperactivity warning required.

regulatory_basis: BPOM Regulation No. 11 of 2019 — Food Colours
notes: Indonesia sets lower limits than Codex for some synthetic colours. Full colour list in BPOM Regulation.

regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code — White Colour Additives
notes: Permitted in South Korea. No ban equivalent to EU August 2022 ban. MFDS monitoring genotoxicity data.

regulatory_basis: UAE.S/GSO Standards for Food Additives — INS 171 permitted
notes: UAE permits TiO2 (E171) as per Codex GSFA. No ban in GCC countries. Halal status: TiO2 is inherently Halal.

regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code — Metals Standards for Food
notes: Korea Food Code sets comprehensive metal limits across all food categories, largely aligned with Codex.

regulatory_basis: BPOM Regulation No. 5 of 2018 — Maximum Limits for Metal Contaminants
notes: Indonesia's contaminant regulations are being progressively updated to align with Codex. BPOM publishes separate contaminant limits by food category.

regulatory_basis: Thai FDA Notification on Contaminants in Food — Metal Contaminants
notes: Thailand has specific limits for seafood (major export). Thai FDA updates contaminant standards regularly.

regulatory_basis: UAE.S 149 — Drinking Water Quality Standard
notes: UAE drinking water standard aligned with WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality (4th edition).

regulatory_basis: GSO 1016 — Contaminants in Food
notes: Saudi Arabia and GCC apply GSO standards for contaminants. GSO 1016 covers heavy metals across food categories.

regulatory_basis: NOM-243-SSA1-2010 — Contaminants in Food and Water
notes: Mexico has specific limits under NOM standards. Some categories stricter than Codex.

regulatory_basis: ANVISA RDC 722/2022 — Contaminants in Food
notes: Brazil updated its contaminant limits via ANVISA RDC 722/2022, largely aligning with Codex.

regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code — Mycotoxin Standards
notes: Korea sets aflatoxin B1 limit at 10 μg/kg for most foods; 2 μg/kg for infant formula — aligned with Codex.

regulatory_basis: BPOM Regulation No. 5 of 2018 — Mycotoxin Limits
notes: Indonesia applies total aflatoxin limit (B1+B2+G1+G2). Significant enforcement challenge given tropical climate favouring mould growth.

regulatory_basis: GSO 1: 2001 — Aflatoxin Limits in Food
notes: GCC applies GSO standards for mycotoxins. Saudi Arabia actively enforces mycotoxin testing at import.

regulatory_basis: NAFDAC Maximum Limits for Aflatoxins in Foods
notes: Nigeria has some of the strictest aflatoxin limits in Africa at 4 μg/kg for AFB1. Enforcement remains a challenge with high mycotoxin burden in domestic grains.

regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code — Microbiological Standards
notes: Korea applies zero tolerance for Salmonella in RTE foods. Mandatory testing for export certificates.

regulatory_basis: SNI (Indonesian National Standard) for Poultry Products
notes: Zero tolerance for Salmonella in all poultry and processed food products. Halal slaughter also mandated.

regulatory_basis: UAE.S 3090 — Microbiological Criteria for Foods
notes: UAE zero tolerance for Salmonella follows GSO and Codex standards. Dubai Municipality conducts active port surveillance testing.

regulatory_basis: Korea Health Functional Food Code — Microbiological Standards
notes: Korea sets strict microbial limits for health functional foods equivalent to pharmaceutical standards.

regulatory_basis: Korea Health Functional Food Code — Nutrient Reference Values
notes: Korea uses RNI (Recommended Nutrient Intake). % NRV labelling uses these values. Upper limits set by MFDS.

regulatory_basis: Korea Health Functional Food Code — NRVs for Labelling
notes: Korean NRV for Vitamin C is 100 mg/day (higher than EU's 80 mg and India's 40 mg).

regulatory_basis: Korean Nutrient Reference Value per MFDS — Food Labeling Standards
notes: Korean NRV for sodium: 2000 mg/day. High sodium warning label triggered at >120 mg/100g.

regulatory_basis: NOM-051-SCFI/SSA1-2010 — Daily Reference Values for Mexico
notes: Mexico NRV: 2000 mg/day sodium. Front-of-pack black octagonal warning seal mandatory if sodium >300 mg per 100g solid or >150 mg/100mL liquid.

regulatory_basis: ANVISA RDC 429/2020 — Nutritional Labeling of Packaged Foods
notes: Brazil DRV: 2400 mg/day sodium. ANVISA adopted warning label triangles for excess nutrients (fat, sugar, sodium) per RDC 429/2020.

regulatory_basis: ANVISA RDC 269/2005 — Dietary Reference Intakes for Brazil
notes: Brazil IDR (Ingestão Diária Recomendada): Vitamin C 45 mg/day. ANVISA updated DRVs per RDC 429/2020.

regulatory_basis: UAE.S/GSO 2233 — Food Additives in Dairy Products
notes: UAE/GCC apply GSO standards for food additives in dairy. Expressed as sorbic acid.

regulatory_basis: NOM-187-SSA1/SCFI-2002 — Masa and Tortilla; COFEPRIS Additives List
notes: Mexico follows Codex GSFA for most additive limits. NOM standards apply to specific product categories.

regulatory_basis: MAPA Monograph for Glyphosate — ANVISA Toxicology Re-evaluation 2019
notes: Brazil is the world's largest soybean producer and glyphosate user. ANVISA completed its re-evaluation in 2019, maintaining registration but adding monitoring requirements.

regulatory_basis: Korean Pesticide MRL Notification — MFDS PLS (Positive List System)
notes: Korea adopted Positive List System (PLS) in 2019 — any pesticide not listed defaults to 0.01 mg/kg MRL. This affects imports significantly.

regulatory_basis: Turkish Food Codex Pesticide Residues Regulation — Aligned with EU Reg 396/2005
notes: Turkey aligned with EU pesticide MRLs as part of customs union obligations. EU ban on chlorpyrifos (October 2020) flows through to Turkish regulations.

regulatory_basis: ANVISA RDC 722/2022 — Contaminants and Mycotoxins in Food
notes: Brazil's updated contaminant regulation (2022) sets comprehensive mycotoxin limits aligned with Codex. Significant enforcement at borders for nut imports.

regulatory_basis: KEBS KS EAS 39:2000 — Maximum Limits for Mycotoxins in Grains
notes: Kenya historically had severe aflatoxin problems in maize. KEBS enforces limits but post-harvest management remains a major challenge.

regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code — Microbiological Standards (Fishery Products)
notes: Korea sets a 100 CFU/g limit for Listeria in some RTE fish products (compared to EU zero tolerance for vulnerable population foods). Products intended for vulnerable populations: absent per 25g.

regulatory_basis: Turkish Food Codex Contaminants Regulation — Aligned with EU 1881/2006
notes: Turkey aligns mycotoxin limits with EU Regulation 1881/2006. Strict enforcement at export/import for nuts — major Turkish export product (hazelnuts, pistachios).

regulatory_basis: SANS 3:2020 — Microbiological and Chemical Requirements for Wine
notes: South Africa is a major wine exporter. OTA in wine aligns with EU/OIV (International Organisation of Vine and Wine) limits.

regulatory_basis: Korea Food Code — Metal Contaminants in Fishery Products
notes: Korea sets mercury at 1.0 mg/kg for predatory fish (tuna, shark). Advisory for pregnant women to limit consumption.

regulatory_basis: UAE.S/GSO 2233 — Contaminants in Fish and Fishery Products
notes: UAE follows GSO/Codex limits for mercury in fish. Gulf fish (e.g. King Mackerel) are frequently tested due to high mercury levels.
